items.gist: The passage maps sacred pithas and sites onto bodily locations from the abdomen down to the feet.
It prescribes constant remembrance that only Shaktis exist as oneself, with no dependence on calendrical or ascetic rules.
It names the nine yoginis and their consorts for the ninefold rite, with the wheel-bearing one central.
Kundalini, seated at the root, pervades everywhere and is worshipped as the central Kuleshvari.
It describes worship of triads, including the heart, eyebrow center, and related triadic sets.
It prescribes cremation-ground seats, yogini groups, and lamps or offerings made in the center.
It rejects dualistic mantras and says the unenduring elements are abandoned in this non-dual rite.
It promises attainment through the rite, effortless mantra success, and recitation of the pitha hymn.
It directs worship of paired forms and avadhutas, and the Kaula lord nourishing Shaktis as universal form.
It denies a fixed sequence in luminous consciousness and rejects separate discussion of ritual branches.
It gives graduated japa counts tied to bodily centers, with homa as a tenth part.
It identifies the self with matrka and Shiva in the body and warns against conceptual division.
It teaches abandonment of pure/impure distinctions and describes japa, homa, and tenfold homa.
It prescribes brahmacarya and distinguishes those who lack bliss from true practitioners.
It defines the marks of Shakti and summarizes six Shaktis yielding enjoyment and liberation.
It describes mutual worship and nourishment of main and subsidiary circles through expansion and release.
It explains how subsidiary-circle goddesses enter the central consciousness circle and become non-different.
It culminates in the non-dual yamala of quiescent and arisen forms as the supreme Kaula.
